newsitem.title: CHINA: China scraps local govt curbs on small cars - paper.
newsitem.headline: China scraps local govt curbs on small cars - paper.

text.p: China has scrapped a ban by local governments on the use of small passenger cars, the Economic Daily News said on Friday.
The cabinet's State Planning Commission issued a notice recently cancelling restrictions by local governments on the use of "economy cars" to fight regional protectionism, it said.
"Regional protectionism ... does not conform to the pattern of a market economy," the newspaper said. "If this development continues, it would not be beneficial ..."
The move by the commission was also aimed at boosting the development of the domestic car industry, the newspaper said.
Because of serious traffic congestion, some cities have restricted the purchase of small passenger cars by limiting the issue of licence plates and auctioning those they issue for exorbitant prices.
China produced 1.5 million motor vehicles in 1995 and is expected to manufacture 2.7 million in 2000.
China's registered car population was forecast to double to 20 million by 2000 from around 10 million in 1996.
